pool.text: Johann Flierl arrived in Lae as a pioneering Lutheran missionary.
Civilian administration began; Cecil John Levien became District Officer (Kiap).
Levien secured mining rights and formed the Guinea Gold syndicate.
Guinea Airways Limited was established by the Guinea Gold syndicate.
Levien arranged construction of Lae airstrip to support gold mines.
Lae was officially declared a town under the New Guinea Boundaries Ordinance.
Amelia Earhart was last seen departing Lae airport on her trans‑Pacific flight.
Decision made to move the Territory of New Guinea capital to Lae.
Japanese forces occupied Lae during World War II.
Battle of the Bismarck Sea thwarted Japanese reinforcement of Lae.
Japanese troops retreated to Lae and Salamaua after Allied victories.
Lae War Cemetery was created adjacent to the Botanical Gardens.
First properly constituted Local Government of Lae town was established.
Population relocated to temporary settlement after major flood.
Magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck north of Lae.
Magnitude 6.8 earthquake occurred 110 km north of Lae.
Agreement signed for Finschhafen District Hydropower Project.
